clinician.trajectory_summary: A female patient in her 60s presented with a vulvar mass on the left labium minus. Excisional biopsy revealed a 32 mm vulvar adenocarcinoma with cribriform, papillary, and ductal architecture, moderate to high cytological atypia, and mitotic indices of 20-31 per 10 HPF, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion and close or involved surgical margins. Immunohistochemistry studies showed initially strong positivity for estrogen receptor (90-100%), CK7, CAM5.2, and GATA3 with negativity for several other markers, and later a profile positive for CK7, SOX10, p53, and E-cadherin but negative for ER and GATA3. Comprehensive imaging including breast examination, mammary imaging, chest CT, GI studies, whole-body PET, and pelvic MRI identified no other primary tumor or metastases except a 12 mm heterogeneous right inguinal adenopathy. Molecular or genomic testing results and clinical course, treatment plan, or follow-up outcome data were not documented in the source. The morphological and immunohistochemical features combined with negative extensive imaging for other primaries support the diagnosis of AMGT of the vulva.
